one_liner: Compiler-cache wrapper for C, C++, CUDA and Rust with local or cloud storage; skips recompiling unchanged units.
what_it_does: sccache is a ccache-like wrapper: prefix the compiler (sccache gcc -c ...), set CMAKE_<LANG>_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=sccache, or set RUSTC_WRAPPER / build.rustc-wrapper for cargo, and it returns stored outputs when the inputs hash the same. It supports gcc, clang, MSVC, rustc, nvcc, NVC++, hipcc and Wind River diab, and stores results on local disk (default 10 GB) or in S3/R2, GCS, Azure, Redis, Memcached, WebDAV, Alibaba OSS, Tencent COS or the GitHub Actions cache, with multi-level caches. A per-machine background server (spawned on first use, exits after 10 minutes idle) holds the storage connection and statistics; an optional sccache-dist scheduler and build servers add icecream-style distributed compilation with authentication.
how_it_is_fast: Content-addressed result caching: for C/C++ the key is a BLAKE3 digest of the preprocessed source plus the compiler binary hash, language, preprocessor and architecture arguments and environment; for Rust it hashes the source, rustc and sysroot libraries, and the parsed arguments. A hit downloads or copies the stored object instead of compiling, so a shared remote cache lets ephemeral CI runners reuse objects built by earlier jobs. A 'preprocessor cache mode' (ccache's direct mode, added in PR #1882 in 2023 and on by default) records each source's include set so a hit can skip running the preprocessor, but only for GCC/Clang with local disk storage; MSVC and remote backends still preprocess on every lookup.
when_to_use: Ephemeral CI runners with a shared remote cache (S3, GCS, Azure, Redis, GitHub Actions cache) where most C/C++ objects match what main already built, such as the amplihack-rs lint job whose first sccache run hit 85% of C/C++ compiles.
Mixed Rust and C/C++ projects (cmake- or cc-built native dependencies under cargo) that want one cache for rustc and the C/C++ compiler.
CUDA or HIP code built with nvcc, clang or hipcc, which sccache caches alongside C/C++ and Rust.
Windows MSVC builds that can use /Z7 (CMake 3.25+ with CMAKE_MSVC_DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT=Embedded and CMP0141 NEW), as a maintained replacement for clcache.
Teams that want distributed compilation with authentication, TLS and sandboxed build servers on 64-bit Linux or FreeBSD, with Linux, Windows or macOS clients.
when_not_to_use: Local GCC/Clang builds where ccache is available: the only head-to-head (issue #160, 2017, Firefox, Clang 4.0) had fully cached sccache at 107 s wall against 35 s for ccache in direct mode; sccache gained a direct mode in 2023 and the issue was closed without new timings.
Rust workspaces dominated by bin, dylib, cdylib or proc-macro crates, or incremental dev builds: these cannot be cached (the amplihack-rs first run hit only 4% of Rust compiles).
MSVC projects that rely on precompiled headers (/Yc, /Fp) or a shared /Zi PDB: those invocations are marked not cacheable and go to the compiler.

Large GitHub Actions matrices writing concurrently to the GitHub Actions cache: HTTP 429 throttling silently drops writes with no retry (open issue #2821 reports 45-90% write loss with five concurrent writers).
Several sccache servers sharing one local cache directory: the local backend supports only a single server and concurrent servers race and cause spurious build failures.

integration.form: standalone executable (Rust crate; prebuilt x86-64 binaries, package managers, cargo install, or the mozilla-actions/sccache-action GitHub Action)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime for the client; optional storage service (S3, GCS, Azure, Redis, Memcached, WebDAV, GHA cache); OpenSSL for the dist-server feature (can be vendored); bubblewrap or Docker on distributed build servers
integration.min_toolchain: Building sccache needs Rust 1.91.0 (rust-version in Cargo.toml at version 0.19.0); cargo 1.40+ for rustc-wrapper; CMake 3.4+ for compiler launchers, and CMake 3.25+ with CMP0141 for MSVC embedded debug info
integration.platforms: Prebuilt x86-64 binaries for Linux (musl), Windows and macOS, other targets via cargo; distributed build servers must be 64-bit Linux or FreeBSD
integration.thread_safety: One local server handles concurrent compile requests from parallel builds and integrates with the GNU make jobserver; a local disk cache supports only one server at a time.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — wraps the existing compiler without build changes, but MSVC needs /Z7 instead of /Zi, and PCH, shared PDBs, non-lib Rust crates, incremental Rust and GCC/MSVC C++20 modules bypass the cache

gotchas: Absolute paths must match for a hit unless SCCACHE_BASEDIRS is set, so CI jobs with different checkout paths miss each other's entries by default.

Preprocessor cache mode can return stale objects when a header that would have been included did not exist at caching time and appears later, or when ignore_time_macros is on; it turns itself off for sources containing __DATE__, __TIME__ or __TIMESTAMP__.
If the client cannot reach its server the build fails by default; set SCCACHE_IGNORE_SERVER_IO_ERROR=1 to fall back to the real compiler.
SCCACHE_C_CUSTOM_CACHE_BUSTER separates C/C++ caches between incompatible invocations, but there is no equivalent for Rust.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick sccache over clcache for any MSVC build that needs a maintained tool or remote storage, and over distcc or icecream when you want cached results reused across machines and runs rather than only farming out compiles (sccache-dist also covers distribution, with authentication). For local-only GCC/Clang builds the catalog has no evidence that it beats ccache.
verified_claims_summary: One third-party CI measurement (amplihack-rs PR #1571, merged 2026-10-16): a GitHub Actions dev-profile cargo build that also compiles the C++ library lbug through cmake took 17 min 26 s on an uncached main run, 6 min 23 s on the PR's first run with sccache and the GitHub Actions cache backend (C/C++ objects mostly already cached by main's clippy step: 1,803 hits, 319 misses; Rust 10 hits, 223 misses; 219 write errors), and 2 min 46 s on a rerun, about 2.7x and 6.3x (derived from page data). Runner hardware, compiler and sccache versions are not stated and the baseline is a different workflow run, though four other uncached main runs spent 763 to 1,062 s in the same doc-review step against 384 s and 168 s with sccache, so the gap exceeds run-to-run spread.
status_note: Actively maintained Mozilla project (version 0.19.0 on main, 7.8k stars, Apache-2.0) with prebuilt binaries, so it can be adopted without building it; the GitHub Actions backend's dropped-write bug (#2821) and its retry PR (#2911) are still open.
